title: Prompt to answer
fullTitle: What Happens Between Your Prompt and the Answer?

captions.text: "How many open support tickets are high priority?" → 5
Between question and number sit several parts. The model is only one.
The application assembles: system message, question, one tool definition.
countTickets(status, priority). Nothing else is offered.
The model does not answer. It requests the tool.
countTickets({status: "open", priority: "high"}) — the request, not private reasoning.
Validate against the schema: tool offered? values allowed? nothing extra?
Unknown tool or unexpected key: refused before anything runs.
Data scope comes from the session, never from the model.
A model-supplied accountId is rejected, and ignored anyway.
The tool runs: narrow, read-only. Two filters + the session's org.
No SQL. The model never touches the data store.
Structured result: { count: 5 } returns to the application, then to the model.
One opaque request id links every step.
Final answer embeds the computed count: 5.
13 open high-priority tickets exist across all orgs; this user sees only their own 5.
Tool failure: one bounded retry (safe only because the tool is read-only).
Still failing: honest message, no count. Nothing invented.
One application design, not every AI request.
The model requests the tool. The application controls execution.
